transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Amy Held.
Iran's Supreme Leader says his country will respond forcefully if anyone attacks.
This, as the U.S. and Israel say, they are preparing for a potential return to hostilities after the midterm elections next week.
NPR's Hadil El-Shalci reports.
Ayatollah Monashtaba Khamenei said that, quote, "any level or type of threat to Iran"
would face a, quote, "immediate and impactful response."
The Supreme Leader made the comments in a meeting with Iranian military officials, according to Iranian state media.
He also ordered the military to update their attack plans with U.S. and Israeli targets.
This comes at a time when Iran has intensified its attacks on ships trying to cross the Strait of Hormuz.
According to Iranian state media, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said that on Friday, four tankers,
one of which was carrying two million barrels of oil, caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait.
Hadil El-Shalci, NPR News, Istanbul.
Just three days remain until the midterms in the U.S. and the money's flowing for the final days of messaging.
An NPR analysis finds a competitive house landscape comprises 70 districts,
where both parties are investing at least six figures in each.
That includes more than $10 million each in toss-up districts in Michigan, North Carolina, New York and Florida.
NPR's Ron Elving reports Democrats have been outspent in almost every race.
They're battling almost limitless resources from Republican donors such as Elon Musk.
Multiple sources say that he has spent over $350 million on this cycle overall.
So the Democrats hope that voters will still be able to get information.
That's NPR's Ron Elving reporting.
Virginia, Washington, D.C., and veterans are suing to stop the Trump administration
from building a massive arch in the nation's capital.
NPR's Stephen Besaha reports.
The Trump administration plans to break ground for the 250-foot arch near Arlington Cemetery
as early as November 5th, assuming approval by the National Capital Planning Commission.
But in a new court filing Saturday, Virginia and D.C. called the plan illegal,
since the administration does not have approval from Congress
and that the arch would be nearly double the city's height limit.
A group of Vietnam War veterans have also sued,
saying the arch would disrupt the sight lines between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington House.
President Trump has said he wants the arch both as a memorial
and a military complex to store drones and station snipers.
Stephen Besaha, NPR News, Birmingham, Alabama.
A federal judge in Florida has once again dismissed Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal
and Rupert Murdoch over an article about a birthday card to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
The newspaper said it featured a crude drawing signed by Trump.
The case is dismissed with prejudice, meaning it cannot be refiled.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. local tomorrow for most of the U.S.
Clocks go back one hour.
But an AP Newark poll finds just 12 percent of Americans are in favor of the time change.
Despite years of attempts in Congress to end it, there's still no agreement on how.
The deciding Game 7 of the WNBA Finals tips off tonight
between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream.
Anna Thorsen from member station KQED reports.
After her team lost Game 6 on Thursday, Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase said
her players hadn't executed very well, but she was confident they would be ready for Game 7.
The physicality is supposed to be ramped up. These are win or die.
This is do or die. This is it.
Whichever team wins, it'll be a milestone for their franchise.
The Atlanta Dream have been to the Finals three times, most recently in 2013.
But they've never won. The Golden State Valkyries have never been to the Finals,
but this is only their second season in existence.
The Valkyries hope to get an edge from an enthusiastic home crowd
that's already made them the most valuable franchise in the WNBA.
For NPR News, I'm Nina Thorsen.
Its legs are small, but its reach is large.
The Dachshund, an icon off the leash, is a new art exhibit getting underway today in Germany.
Known as sausage dogs, they're featured in paintings, drawings, videos,
and stuffed toys shown at the art show.
Organizers say there will even be time for Dachshunds themselves
to come by for a look and a sniff.
This is NPR News.
That's plus dot NPR dot org.

topics.text: Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei warns of forceful response to any threat amid Hormuz attacks
NPR analysis finds 70 competitive House districts where both parties invest heavily before midterms
Virginia and D.C. sue to block Trump administration's 250-foot arch near Arlington Cemetery
Federal judge dismisses Trump's defamation lawsuit against Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch with prejudice
Daylight saving time ends tomorrow; AP-NORC poll finds just 12 percent favor the time change
Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream face off in deciding Game 7 of WNBA Finals
Dachshund art exhibit opens in Germany featuring sausage dog paintings, videos, and stuffed toys
